title: Hodge–Tate theory, canonical subgroups, and automorphic period maps
summary: Complete whole-roadmap target-level plan of all nine layers. It imports, unchanged and hash-pinned, the two accepted part packets (T0–T5: 66 targets; T6, T6:log-sites, T6:comparison: 68 targets) and adds 4 targets. The additions put the roadmap in the Caraiani–Newton upstream order (tier 16): the p-level Shimura tower, its right G(ℚ_p)-action and the infinite-level diamond move down from PerfectoidShimuraVarieties S0 (tier 17) into T2, and the Andreatta–Iovita–Pilloni comparison is stated at torsor level in T5 (Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams Lemma 7.12 and diagram (7.2)), leaving the sheaf-level Theorem 7.14 to OverconvergentAutomorphicForms O5, which is outside the order. Effective prerequisites of imported targets, six field corrections (four of them complete the coverage of the maintainer-added sources), the 47 maintainer-added source items and the six handed red-team findings are recorded explicitly. The roadmap builds Fargues degrees and the finite Hodge–Tate map (T0), the abelian relative comparison (T1), Hodge–Tate sequences, flags, Levi torsors and the open-tower period map (T2), canonical subgroups with bounds (T3), canonical/anticanonical loci and BHW period estimates (T4), Igusa torsors, ω^int, ω^mod and the AIP torsor (T5), and logarithmic adic sites, logarithmic periods and finite-level canonical comparison (T6). Every stage is planned, none closed; nothing is implemented.

nodes.title: The p-level tower of a Shimura datum at fixed tame level
nodes.statement: Let (G, X) be a pure Shimura datum with reflex field E for which ShimuraVarieties V8 supplies actual canonical models together with their descended level maps and minimal compactifications; this holds for data of abelian type through V6 and V8/abelian-instance, which include the Siegel, PEL, Hodge-type and Hilbert data of T2–T5. Fix a prime p, a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field C of characteristic 0 over ℚ_p, an embedding ι: E → C and a compact open subgroup K^p ⊂ G(𝔸_f^p). Let CO_p be the set of compact open subgroups of G(ℚ_p) ordered by inclusion; it is nonempty (intersect a closed faithful embedding G(ℚ_p) ⊂ GL_d(ℚ_p) with GL_d(ℤ_p)) and cofiltered because K_p ∩ K′_p is again compact open. The p-level tower at tame level K^p is the functor on CO_p that sends K_p to the analytic adic space S_{K_p} := (Sh_{K^pK_p}(G, X) ⊗_{E,ι} C)^{ad} over Spa(C, O_C), and an inclusion K′_p ⊆ K_p to the analytification π_{K′_p,K_p}: S_{K′_p} → S_{K_p} of the descended forgetful map. The compactified tower K_p ↦ S*_{K_p} := (Sh^{min}_{K^pK_p}(G, X) ⊗_{E,ι} C)^{ad}, with the extended level maps, contains the open tower as the complement of the boundary, functorially in K_p. Every transition map is finite, and on the open tower it is finite étale when K^pK_p is neat. If σ: C ≅ ℂ is an isomorphism of abstract fields (one exists exactly when C has the cardinality of the continuum, for instance C = ℂ_p), then through σ ∘ ι the C-points are S_{K_p}(C) = G(ℚ)\(X × G(𝔸_f)/K^pK_p), compatibly with the transition maps.
hypotheses: (G, X) lies in the class of data whose canonical models and level maps are supplied: abelian type, through V6 and V8/abelian-instance. General data with the V7/V8.general models are handled by PerfectoidShimuraVarieties S0.general, which builds on this node.

C is complete, algebraically closed and of characteristic 0 over ℚ_p, and the tower depends on ι. Descent of the tower to E_v or to another finite extension of ℚ_p is a separate statement, not part of this notation.
Neatness is needed only for étaleness; finiteness of the level maps holds without it (ShimuraVarieties:V8/finite-level-maps).

The general compact-open level index category of V8/level-tower is an explicit gap recorded in that packet. This node uses only its restriction to the levels K^pK_p with K^p fixed, indexed by the poset CO_p of subgroups of G(ℚ_p).
proofSteps: Restrict the algebraic tower of ShimuraVarieties:V8/level-tower and its finite level maps (V8/finite-level-maps, instantiated for abelian type by V8/abelian-instance) to the levels K^pK_p with K_p ∈ CO_p. Base change along ι and apply the analytification functor of AdicSpacesPartII R1, which preserves finite and étale morphisms (R1/analytification-finite, R1/analytification-etale-smooth).

For the compactified tower use the projective normal models over E of V8/minimal-descent and the finite extended level maps of V8/minimal-map-extension. The level maps carry boundary to boundary and interior to interior, so the open tower is the complement of the boundary termwise and functorially.

Identity and composition laws are inherited from the algebraic tower. For the points, base change of the canonical models along σ ∘ ι is the complex Shimura variety, whose points are the double cosets of ShimuraVarieties:V1/analytic-points; an identity between algebraic maps that holds over ℂ holds over E, hence after base change to any C, so no identification of C with ℂ is needed beyond the points statement.

nodes.title: The right action of G(ℚ_p) and the prime-to-p Hecke translations on the p-level tower
nodes.statement: In the situation of T2/p-level-tower, let g ∈ G(ℚ_p), embedded in G(𝔸_f) with trivial prime-to-p component, and K_p ∈ CO_p. The analytified descended right translation T_g: S_{K_p} → S_{g⁻¹K_pg} (on complex points before descent, [x, a] ↦ [x, ag]) is an isomorphism, and it extends to the compactified tower. These isomorphisms satisfy T_1 = id, T_{gh} = T_h ∘ T_g, and π ∘ T_g = T_g ∘ π for the transition maps π; for k ∈ K_p the map T_k on S_{K_p} is the identity. Hence, for K′_p normal in K_p, the finite group K_p/K′_p acts on S_{K′_p} over S_{K_p}, and G(ℚ_p) acts on the right on the pro-system (S_{K_p})_{K_p}, an action in the sense of Deligne. For h ∈ G(𝔸_f^p) the translations S_{K^pK_p} → S_{h⁻¹K^phK_p} commute with all T_g and all transition maps.
hypotheses: As in T2/p-level-tower; g ranges over all of G(ℚ_p), not only over a compact open subgroup.

The action is C-linear because it is formed after base change along ι. Scholze's spaces over ℚ_p^cycl carry a GSp_{2g}(ℚ_p)-action that moves the structure map to Spa(ℚ_p^cycl) (torsion paper, footnote 7); that twisted form is a different object and is not this action.
proofSteps: Base change along ι and analytify the descended algebraic right translations of ShimuraVarieties:V8/translation-laws and their extensions to minimal models (V8/minimal-map-extension).

The identities T_1 = id, T_{gh} = T_h ∘ T_g and T_k = id for k ∈ K_p are the translation laws of V8; on complex points they are the double-coset formulas of V1/right-translation. Identities of algebraic maps descend from ℂ to E and survive base change to C and analytification.

Commutation with transition maps and with prime-to-p translations is the same double-coset computation: [x, a] ↦ [x, ag] and [x, a] ↦ [x, ah] commute because g and h are supported at disjoint sets of places.

nodes.title: The infinite-level Shimura diamond S^◇_{K^p,∞}
nodes.statement: In the situation of T2/p-level-tower, put S^◇_{K^p,∞} := lim_{K_p} (S_{K_p})^◇ and S^{*◇}_{K^p,∞} := lim_{K_p} (S*_{K_p})^◇, limits of v-sheaves on perfectoid spaces over Spd(C, O_C) of the diamonds of DiamondsAndVStacks D6; no perfectoidness is assumed. Then: (i) S^{*◇}_{K^p,∞} is a spatial diamond, its projections to the finite levels are quasicompact and quasiseparated, and |S^{*◇}_{K^p,∞}| → lim_{K_p} |S*_{K_p}| is a homeomorphism; (ii) S^◇_{K^p,∞} is the open subdiamond over the complement of the boundary, a locally spatial diamond with |S^◇_{K^p,∞}| ≅ lim_{K_p} |S_{K_p}|; (iii) for a perfectoid (R, R⁺) over (C, O_C), S^◇_{K^p,∞}(R, R⁺) = lim_{K_p} S_{K_p}(R, R⁺); (iv) the right action of T2/tower-right-action induces a right action of G(ℚ_p) on S^◇_{K^p,∞} and S^{*◇}_{K^p,∞}, continuous on compact open subgroups (each K_p acts on the K′_p-stage through the finite quotient K_p/K′_p for K′_p normal in K_p); (v) when K^pK_p is neat, S^◇_{K^p,∞} → (S_{K_p})^◇ is separated and quasi-pro-étale: after pullback to a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid test space it is represented by the pro-étale limit of the finite étale covers above K_p. A cofinal family of levels gives a canonically isomorphic limit.
hypotheses: The limit is formed in v-sheaves over Spd(C, O_C) along the cofiltered poset CO_p, or along any family of levels that is initial in it.
S*_{K_p} is the analytification of a projective variety, hence quasicompact and quasiseparated; this gives spatiality in (i). The open tower is only locally spatial.
proofSteps: Each (S*_{K_p})^◇ is a spatial diamond and each (S_{K_p})^◇ a locally spatial diamond, with the same underlying topological space as the adic space (DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/etale-site-comparison, D5/spatial-diamond).

The transition maps are finite, hence quasicompact and quasiseparated. Scholze's limit lemma (DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons, ECD Lemma 11.22) gives (i). For (ii) the preimage of the open complement of the boundary is an open subdiamond (D4/underlying-topological-space), and the same lemma applies to the open tower.
(iii) is the evaluation of a limit of sheaves on Spd(R, R⁺), using the description of the diamond functor on perfectoid test objects (D6/gluing-and-the-diamond-functor).

(iv): the T_g commute with the transition maps, so they induce maps of limits; a compact open K_p acts on each stage S_{K′_p} with K′_p normal in K_p through the finite group K_p/K′_p, hence continuously.

(v): pull back along a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid T → (S_{K_p})^◇. The finite étale covers at finer levels become finite étale affinoid perfectoid spaces over T. Their limit is affinoid perfectoid by PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces (ECD Proposition 6.5); its map to T is pro-étale, since over every rank-one point its fibre is that point times an inverse limit of finite discrete sets (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/pro-etale-maps-over-std-base, ECD Lemma 7.19). The projection is separated as a limit of separated maps. This proves quasi-pro-étaleness by DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-quasi-pro-etale-morphisms-of-stacks (ECD Definition 10.1 and Convention 10.2). Independence of the cofinal family uses mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limitIso.

nodes.title: The Hodge–Tate section compares the anticanonical tower with the AIP torsor
nodes.statement: Let F be the totally real field of the Hilbert datum, m ≥ 1, let ε lie in the range of T5/hodge-tate-aip-lift (ε ≤ p^{−(m+1)}, inside the level-m canonical range), and let n ∈ ℤ_{≥1} ∪ {∞}. Write X_n := X_{Γ*(p^∞)}(p^nε)_a for the anticanonical full-level tower at radius p^nε (X_∞ := X_{Γ*(p^∞)}(ε)_a), u_n: X_n → X_{Γ*(p^∞)}(ε)_a for the morphism given by the action of the matrix diag(p^n, 1) (BHW §7.2; u_∞ = id), and s̃_n := s ∘ u_n, where s = HT(α(e₁)) is the canonical Hodge–Tate section factored through the AIP torsor F_m(ε) ⊂ T(ω) by T5/hodge-tate-aip-lift. Then: (i) s̃_n is a morphism over the Atkin–Lehner isomorphism AL_n: X_{Γ₀*(p^n)}(p^nε)_a ≅ X(ε) of T4/atkin-lehner-anticanonical, that is, the projection of F_m(ε) to X(ε) composed with s̃_n equals AL_n composed with the projection of X_n to Γ₀*(p^n)-level (for n = ∞, the forgetful map X_{Γ₀*(p^∞)}(ε)_a → X(ε)); (ii) for γ = (a b; c d) in the deck group Γ₀*(p^n) of X_n over its Γ₀*(p^n)-quotient (for n = ∞, for every γ in Γ₀*(p)), the factor j(γ, x) := c·z(x) + d, with z the Hodge–Tate coordinate of T4/hodge-tate-coordinate on X_n, takes values in the AIP structure group B_m, and s̃_n(x·γ) = j(γ, x)·s̃_n(x) for the B_m-torsor action on F_m(ε), the action of γ on X_n being the one of BHW's diagram (7.2) in the conventions of T4/hodge-tate-coordinate; (iii) consequently, for a bounded smooth weight κ: U → 𝒲* and a section f of 𝒪_{F_m(ε)×U} with b*f = κ⁻¹(b)·f for all b ∈ B_m, the pullback g = s̃_n* f satisfies γ*g = κ⁻¹(c·z + d)·g for every γ ∈ Γ₀*(p^n), and s̃_n* carries 𝒪⁺-valued eigenfunctions to 𝒪⁺-valued functions. The identification of the resulting coefficient sheaves (Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams, Theorem 7.14) and its Hecke equivariance are OverconvergentAutomorphicForms O5/O6 theorems built on this one.
hypotheses: Conventions of T4/hodge-tate-coordinate: dual-abelian Hilbert level structures α: 𝒪_p² ≅ T_pA^∨, the kernel coordinate z and the left fractional-linear action, with the conversion α′ = α ∘ γ^∨ to the right action on the tower fixed there.

B_m is the actual structure group of the étale torsor F_m(ε) → X(ε) of T5/aip-torsor. That j lands in B_m is the ratio argument of T5/aip-automorphy-factor; the containment printed as (7.1) in BHW holds only in the corrected direction recorded in the T0–T5 part's source issues and is not used backwards.

The level m attached to a weight follows the corrected indexing of the T0–T5 part (m = k + r − 1 on the k-th piece of weight space); (iii) is stated for any κ whose analytic extension is admitted on B_m.

Finite n uses the scaled radius p^nε with p^nε < 1/2, as required by T4/atkin-lehner-anticanonical. In the Hilbert case retain the canonical-subgroup range at each quotient step required by that supplier. Level zero is recovered downstream for coefficient sheaves through AL_1 (BHW Theorem 7.14, proof, p. 31); it does not assert equivariance of this anticanonical branch under Γ₀*(1) = G*(ℤ_p).
proofSteps: For n = ∞: T5/hodge-tate-aip-lift gives the factorization s: X_∞ → F_m(ε). The square over X(ε) commutes because the projection of s(x) is the abelian variety underlying x (BHW Lemma 7.12, right square). The left square, s(x·γ) = j(γ, x)·s(x) with j in B_m, is T5/aip-automorphy-factor.

For finite n ≥ 1, put ρ = u_n γ u_n⁻¹ = (a p^n b; p^{−n} c d). Its lower-left entry need not be divisible by p, so do not apply the Γ₀*(p) assertion of T5/aip-automorphy-factor to ρ. Instead the general quotient-line transformation of T4/hodge-tate-coordinate on the two charts gives z(u_n x) = p^n z(x) and j(ρ,u_n x) = (p^{−n}c)(p^n z(x)) + d = cz(x)+d. The two transformed HT lifts lie in F_m(ε) by T5/hodge-tate-aip-lift and over the same point of X(ε), since γ fixes the Γ₀*(p^n) quotient and u_n lies over AL_n. Their unique ratio in that faithfully acting torsor is therefore cz+d, which proves membership in B_m and equivariance. The right square is T4/atkin-lehner-anticanonical. This interprets BHW diagram (7.2) with the finite-level group Γ₀*(p^n) used in the proof of Theorem 7.14, rather than the Γ₀*(p) printed in the diagram.
(iii) is formal from (ii): for f with b*f = κ⁻¹(b)f, g(x·γ) = f(j(γ, x)·s̃_n(x)) = κ⁻¹(j(γ, x))·g(x). Integrality is preserved because s̃_n is a morphism of adic spaces and pullback preserves 𝒪⁺.
acceptance: For n = ∞ and diagonal γ = diag(a, d) ∈ Γ₀*(p), (ii) reads s(x·γ) = d·s(x), matching the transformation ψ ↦ dψ of the Igusa generator in T5/igusa-full-level-comparison.
For κ(t) = t^k on 𝒪_p^× (an algebraic weight), (iii) gives γ*g = (c·z + d)^{−k}·g, the weight-k automorphy law on the anticanonical tower.
The statement makes no claim that the pulled-back eigenfunctions span an invertible 𝒪⁺-module or that the induced map of coefficient sheaves is an isomorphism; both are O5's.

The level restriction is necessary: at an ordinary point with z = 0, the Weyl matrix (0 −1; 1 0) belongs to G*(ℤ_p) = Γ₀*(1) and sends the kernel line to ∞, outside the chosen anticanonical chart. It cannot be treated as a deck transformation preserving this branch.

leanPrototype.readerParagraph: `research/blueprint/suggested/HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups.lean` (780 lines) is written to the 2026-10-12 shape. It states and does not develop. Its light real-bodied definitions use carriers that exist at the pins: the affine conormal module (Tau Ceti's cotangent space of a bialgebra), the compact open subgroups that index the p-level tower, the Hasse valuation and the weak, strong and BHW ranges with c_p, the fractional-linear action with its factor cz + d, the AIP exponent x = m − εp^m/(p − 1), and prelog and log structures on a ring. The six milestones are: intersections of compact open subgroups are compact open, the level poset is cofiltered, the strong range implies the weak one, the cocycle of cz + d, the action law, and the trivial log structure is a log structure; the first and last are proved outright. Ten examples evaluate c_p, S_n, the AIP exponent and the identity matrix, separate the weak range from the strong one, and show that the one-element monoid is not a log structure on ℚ. Every other planned declaration (707 distinct names across 771 index entries) is listed in a closing index by layer and target, because its carrier (Shimura towers and diamonds, p-divisible groups over valuation rings, semi-abelian degenerations, period sheaves, log adic sites, the AIP torsor) is not at the pins. `lean-check` at Mathlib 082e2d37e8 and Tau Ceti f790474 exits 0 with four warnings, all for proofs left open. The part files `HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups--T0.lean` and `--T6.lean` keep their fuller typed prototypes.
